---
title: 'Agentic E2E Framework (`e2e`)'
description: 'Write, record, replay, and run deterministic end-to-end tests with e2e, committed .e2e/cache traces, headless Chromium rules, and npx --no-install e2e mcp for coding agents.'
updatedAt: '2026-11-27'
audience: developers
---

Tuturuuu adopts [`e2e`](https://github.com/e2e-inc/e2e) (npm `e2e` +
`@e2e-dev/web`, Apache-2.0) alongside the existing Playwright suites under
`apps/web/e2e/`. Existing Playwright configurations and specs stay untouched;
new `e2e` tests live under `apps/web/e2e-agent/` and replay from committed
`.e2e/cache/` recordings in CI with zero model calls.

## Shared configuration and headless rules

The repository root [`e2e.config.ts`](https://github.com/tutur3u/platform/blob/main/e2e.config.ts)
delegates to
[`scripts/e2e/shared-web-config.ts`](https://github.com/tutur3u/platform/blob/main/scripts/e2e/shared-web-config.ts),
which enforces Tuturuuu's web headless browser rules:

- **Playwright Chromium, headless by default.** Pass `--headed` only for local
  interactive debugging, never in CI.
- **No User-Agent spoofing or challenge bypasses.** The config leaves
  `userAgent` and bypass headers unset so adaptive abuse controls
  (`ABUSE_CHALLENGE_REQUIRED`) and Cloudflare Turnstile remain authentic. See
  [QA test users](/build/development-tools/qa-test-users).
- **Credential and trace hygiene.** `video` is `'off'` and `trace` is
  `'retain-on-failure'` so session cookies and secrets are never captured in
  routine uploads. Local `.e2e/results/` failure traces are gitignored; do not
  share them when running locally with real credentials.
- **Stable project and app identity.** `projectId: 'tuturuuu-platform'` and
  `app.identity: 'tuturuuu-web'` keep loopback replay cache keys identical
  across worktrees and dynamic loopback ports (`e2e` keys non-loopback hosts
  under `environment: 'production'` unless `app.environment` is set explicitly,
  so committed traces apply to the deterministic loopback `test` environment).
- **Fail-closed offline default.** `e2e.config.ts` uses `offlineReplayExecutor`,
  which refuses uncached steps instead of calling any external API. Committed
  `.e2e/cache/` entries replay before the executor is invoked.

## Fleet test identity from environment variables only

Never commit emails, passwords, TOTP seeds, or session cookies in tests,
configs, or `.e2e/cache/` files. `shared-web-config.ts` resolves the `fleet`
identity strictly from environment variable names:

| Role | Environment variable names (checked in order) |
| --- | --- |
| Fleet email | `E2E_SECRET_FLEET_EMAIL`, `E2E_USER_FLEET_USERNAME`, `E2E_FLEET_EMAIL`, `TUTURUUU_FLEET_SMOKE_EMAIL`, or `TUTURUUU_FLEET_SMOKE_ID` (`qa-automation+<uuid>@smoke.tuturuuu.com`) |
| Fleet password | `E2E_USER_FLEET_PASSWORD`, `E2E_FLEET_PASSWORD`, `TUTURUUU_FLEET_SMOKE_PASSWORD` |

Pass both email and password as opaque `e2e` handles (`secrets.get('fleet-email')`
and `credentials.user('fleet').password`) so `.e2e/cache/` recordings store only
secret names (`fleet-email`, `fleet.password`) and resolve values dynamically at
replay time.

## Writing a test

Place new web tests in `apps/web/e2e-agent/*.e2e.ts`. Combine natural-language
`agent.act(...)` steps with deterministic `expect(...)` checks so `e2e` can
verify and cache every action trace:

```ts
import { test } from '@e2e-dev/web';
import { credentials, expect, secrets } from 'e2e';

test('signs in with the fleet test identity from env names only', async ({
  agent,
  app,
  browser,
  screen,
}) => {
  const fleet = credentials.user('fleet');

  await app.open('/en/login');
  await expect(
    screen.getByPlaceholder('Enter your email or username')
  ).toBeVisible();

  await agent.act(
    'enter the fleet email and continue to the password step, then submit the fleet password to sign in',
    {
      params: {
        email: secrets.get('fleet-email'),
        password: fleet.password,
      },
    }
  );

  await expect(browser).toHaveURL(/\/en\/personal(?:\/|$)/);
  await expect(screen.getByRole('heading', 'Personal Workspace')).toBeVisible();
});
```

Every `agent.act()` call must be followed by a deterministic verification
(`expect(locator)...`, `expect(browser).toHaveURL(...)`, or `locator.waitFor()`).
Without a verification check, `e2e` marks the step `unconfirmed` and will not
write a replay cache entry.

## Running and recording `.e2e/cache`

### Verify committed recordings deterministically (zero model calls)

```bash
# Install Chromium for @e2e-dev/web once per machine
bun x e2e-web install chromium --with-deps

# Run against the deterministic loopback fixture server with --strict-cache
CI=1 E2E_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 \
  E2E_SECRET_FLEET_EMAIL="qa-fixture@example.invalid" \
  E2E_USER_FLEET_PASSWORD="ephemeral-local-fixture-password" \
  npx --no-install e2e run --strict-cache
```

To target a running local production build of `apps/web` (`next start` on a
build-allowed host; never a dev server for verification) instead of the
loopback fixture server, set `E2E_APP_URL`:

```bash
E2E_APP_URL=http://localhost:7803 \
  E2E_SECRET_FLEET_EMAIL="..." \
  E2E_USER_FLEET_PASSWORD="..." \
  npx --no-install e2e run --strict-cache
```

Note that the committed fixture recordings expect fixture-shaped data (a board
named `Personal Board` at `/en/personal/tasks/boards/default`, a guest-enabled
room at `/en/r/e2e-guest-room`, and password sign-in without TOTP); targeting a
live deployment with different fixtures or TOTP requires matching test data or
freshly recorded traces.

### Record or refresh a stale trace

When a UI flow intentionally changes, `--strict-cache` fails with
`REPLAY_STALE` (exit code `2`) instead of silently paying for CI model calls.
Because `e2e.config.ts` pins `offlineReplayExecutor` to prevent accidental
model calls, record updated traces with a temporary, uncommitted local config
that calls `createTuturuuuWebE2EConfig` with your model provider or custom
`executor`:

1. Create an untracked local recording config (for example
   `tmp/e2e.record.config.ts`) that spreads or calls
   `createTuturuuuWebE2EConfig` with your configured model/subscription or
   recording executor, then run in `read-write` mode without `--strict-cache`:
   ```bash
   npx --no-install e2e run --config tmp/e2e.record.config.ts apps/web/e2e-agent/<file>.e2e.ts
   ```
2. Delete the temporary config, inspect the recorded cache entries, and verify
   no secrets or personal text were captured verbatim:
   ```bash
   npx --no-install e2e cache ls
   npx --no-install e2e cache stats
   git diff .e2e/cache/
   ```
3. Re-verify zero-model deterministic replay against the committed `e2e.config.ts`
   before committing:
   ```bash
   CI=1 E2E_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 \
     E2E_SECRET_FLEET_EMAIL="qa-fixture@example.invalid" \
     E2E_USER_FLEET_PASSWORD="ephemeral-local-fixture-password" \
     npx --no-install e2e run --strict-cache
   ```

Runtime outputs under `.e2e/` (`report.json`, `junit.xml`, `results/`,
`timings.json`) are gitignored; only `.e2e/cache/` is committed.

## CI workflow (report-only)

`.github/workflows/e2e-framework-report-only.yaml` runs
`npx --no-install e2e run --strict-cache --reporter list,junit` on pull requests
and pushes to `main` that touch the e2e config, suites, fixture server, or cache.

- **Report-only initially:** the job sets `continue-on-error: true` and is not
  a required merge check while suite coverage expands.
- **Zero model calls, zero secrets:** no AI API key or repository secret is
  passed to the workflow. Ephemeral per-run fixture credentials are generated in
  memory for the loopback fixture server.
- **Artifacts:** `.e2e/report.json` and `.e2e/junit.xml` are uploaded for 7
  days; `.e2e/results/` traces upload only on failure.

## Agent MCP setup (`npx --no-install e2e mcp`)

`npx --no-install e2e mcp` exposes a live browser session over stdio so coding
agents can inspect the screen, verify locators, walk flows, and copy verified
test lines directly into `apps/web/e2e-agent/*.e2e.ts` without needing a model
API key.

<Note>
  `.mcp.json` and `.codex/config.*` are gitignored in this repository so local
  agent configs stay machine-specific. Register the server locally using the
  snippets below from the repository root after `bun install`.
</Note>

### Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add --scope project e2e -- npx --no-install e2e mcp
```

Or add to local `.mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "e2e": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["--no-install", "e2e", "mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

### Cursor

Add to `.cursor/mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "e2e": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["--no-install", "e2e", "mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

### Codex

Add to local `.codex/config.toml`:

```toml
[mcp_servers.e2e]
command = "npx"
args = ["--no-install", "e2e", "mcp"]
```

To target a running local `apps/web` server during an MCP session, pass
`E2E_APP_URL=http://localhost:7803` in the MCP server environment.

## Supply-chain notes

`e2e`, `@e2e-dev/core`, and `@e2e-dev/web` are Apache-2.0 packages published via
GitHub Actions OIDC trusted publishing from `e2e-inc/e2e` with SLSA Provenance
v1 attestations and zero lifecycle install scripts (`preinstall`/`install`/`postinstall`).
They are installed through `bun add -D` and obey the repository's
`minimumReleaseAge` policy in `bunfig.toml` without requiring
`trustedDependencies` or release-age exemptions.

## Flutter mobile harness

The mobile suites live in `apps/mobile/e2e/` with an independent Bun manifest
and lockfile. From the repository root, run these commands for config and
discovery checks without a device:

```bash
cd apps/mobile/e2e
bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts
node --test shared-mobile-config.test.mjs
npx --no-install e2e list
npx --no-install e2e cache stats
```

For controls that a spec needs to find, set a stable, locale-independent
`Semantics(identifier: 'shell-workspace-picker')` on the control and use
`screen.getByTestId('shell-workspace-picker')`. Keep Flutter keys, labels and
handlers in place. Use a stable entity ID for repeated controls, as in
`tasks-board-card-<board-id>`. Follow each `agent.act(...)` with an exact
assertion about the resulting UI so the action can be recorded and replayed.

### Device and QA setup

Use a dedicated phone profile on an iOS Simulator or Android Emulator. Supply a prebuilt simulator
`.app` or emulator `.apk` with the identifiers in this checkout. Set
`TUTURUUU_MOBILE_E2E_IOS_APP` or `TUTURUUU_MOBILE_E2E_ANDROID_APP` to its path, or
install the build on the device before starting. Absolute paths also work for
builds outside the harness. Select a specific device with
`TUTURUUU_MOBILE_E2E_IOS_DEVICE` or `TUTURUUU_MOBILE_E2E_ANDROID_DEVICE`. The
default flavor is `dev` (`com.tuturuuu.app.mobile.dev`). Set
`TUTURUUU_MOBILE_E2E_FLAVOR=stg` for `com.tuturuuu.app.mobile.stg`.

Start the login spec on a signed-out device profile. It checks email entry
without submitting the form. The Tasks and Meet specs use an already issued
QA session from the backend the artifact targets. Supply both parts through
the environment:

| Token | Environment variable names in priority order |
| --- | --- |
| Access token | `E2E_SECRET_MOBILE_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `E2E_USER_MOBILE_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `TUTURUUU_MOBILE_QA_ACCESS_TOKEN` |
| Refresh token | `E2E_SECRET_MOBILE_REFRESH_TOKEN`, `E2E_USER_MOBILE_REFRESH_TOKEN`, `TUTURUUU_MOBILE_QA_REFRESH_TOKEN` |

The setup opens the app's existing flavor-specific login callback if the app is
signed out. Use a short-lived session issued through an approved sign-in for a
disposable QA user with Tasks and Meet access and at least one visible board.
Keep both values out of commands, docs, and recordings. The mobile harness
does not submit a password or alter Turnstile. Tasks and Meet explicitly skip
when neither token is present.

### Record and replay

Create a local `apps/mobile/e2e/e2e.record.config.ts` beside the harness config
and export `createTuturuuuMobileE2EConfig({ model })` or
`createTuturuuuMobileE2EConfig({ executor })` with your local provider. Keep that
file and all credentials local. Record one target and spec at a time:

```bash
npx --no-install e2e run --config e2e.record.config.ts --target ios tests/auth.e2e.ts
npx --no-install e2e cache ls
npx --no-install e2e run --target ios --strict-cache tests/auth.e2e.ts
```

Use `--target android` for the emulator. Review the resulting
`.e2e/cache/` diff for sensitive fixture data before committing a recording.
Only that subdirectory is tracked. Cache misses fail with the default offline
executor. CI reads the cache and always uses the offline executor.

Mobile report-only CI runs config tests, discovery and cache checks on admitted
PRs and matching pushes. To try strict replay, dispatch
`mobile-e2e-framework-report-only.yaml` with a platform, flavor, public HTTPS
artifact URL and SHA-256. Supply a ZIP containing `Runner.app` at its root for
the `macos-15` iOS runner or an x86_64-compatible APK for Android. The dispatch
runs the signed-out spec and skips the two specs that require a QA session.
The cache starts empty. Config tests and discovery do not establish native
replay coverage.

### Mobile MCP

With the matching app installed on the selected test device, start
`npx --no-install e2e mcp` from `apps/mobile/e2e/`. In the MCP client call
`open_session` with `target: "ios"` or `target: "android"`, use the session's
device tools to inspect locators, and call `close_session` when finished. MCP
does not need a model key. [Upstream mobile guide](https://e2e.com/docs/mobile).
